title: Largest tropical rainforests
measure: Area of primary forest in km², meaning old-growth forest that hasn't been cleared, measured from satellite data for 2020. Rainforest regions are counted as whole regions that cross borders, such as the Amazon.

entries.name: Amazon
entries.country: Brazil (about 60%), Peru, Colombia and six others
entries.note: More than three times the size of the next rainforest.
entries.source: Mongabay, The world's great rainforests (2020), from University of Maryland and World Resources Institute satellite data

entries.name: Congo
entries.country: DR Congo (60%), Gabon, Republic of the Congo, Cameroon and others
entries.source: Mongabay, The world's great rainforests (2020), from University of Maryland and World Resources Institute satellite data

entries.name: New Guinea and Australia
entries.note: Nearly all on the island of New Guinea.
entries.source: Mongabay, The world's great rainforests (2020), from University of Maryland and World Resources Institute satellite data

entries.name: Sundaland
entries.note: Borneo, Sumatra and the Malay Peninsula. It lost the largest share of its primary forest of any region in the 2000s and 2010s.
entries.source: Mongabay, The world's great rainforests (2020), from University of Maryland and World Resources Institute satellite data
